chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: First Kansas City band with written music
summary: Jesse Stone's Blue Serenaders were the only band with written arrangements, with better harmony than Bennie Moten.

bands.name: Jesse Stone and His Blue Serenaders

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now we were the first band, black band, in Kansas City with music on paper. Everybody was playing head arrangements. We had --
What's the name of this band, now?

This is Jesse Stone and his Blue Serenaders. We were the only band that had music on paper, and we could tear up anybody there. We really had arrangements. And with good harmony, like I mean like Benny Moten and everything, it was heading right then it sound pretty good, but now that I'm transcribing some of that stuff for the New York Jazz
Repertory Company. You could see that the harmony was terrible if you -- you know.
But all of our harmony was beautiful. This man was writing music like a champion then!
He was a new guy. He was the (Bunny) even then.
